newsitem.title: SPAIN: Peseta settles into new range versus mark.
newsitem.headline: Peseta settles into new range versus mark.

text.p: The peseta settled into a new range against the mark in afternoon trade on Tuesday after a strong run since Friday when a break in central bank intervention prompted a jump through the 84.00 per mark barrier.
By 1540 GMT, the peseta was trading at 83.56/59 compared with early trading levels of 83.61/64 and late Monday's levels of 83.47/48.
After easing slightly against the mark in early trade, the peseta remained largely rangebound for much of the afternoon. Traders blamed failure to break a number of key levels.
"Yesterday, the market tried to break the 83.35/40 range but couldn't and so today we tried the same at the other extreme (83.65)," said one trader.
Traders said the market was keenly awaiting Wednesday's CPI data and Thursday's repurchase auction.
However, a decision by the central bank not to cut its key money rate on Thursday, as expected, could spark another climb toward the 83.00 level, traders warned.
Traders say that although the Bank of Spain had been absent from the market since Friday, it would likely step back in if the peseta appreciated toward 83.00 per mark.
